Jamie (AE): Hey team -- BlueHarbor is asking about migrating from GoliathAI's API to Redwood. They want a short POC to prove prompt parity + pricing delta. Major ask: minimal code changes for their engineering org. Any known quick wins?
Tyler (SE): Nice — we can do a compatibility shim. Quick approach: map Goliath's param names -> Redwood equivalents and handle streaming differences. Example shim: 
```
// pseudo
req.model = req.model || 'goliath-2';
redwoodReq.prompt = req.input || req.prompt;
redwoodReq.max_tokens = req.max_tokens || req.length;
// streaming: Goliath uses SSE 'event: token', Redwood streams as 'data' chunks — translate on the client
```
Jamie (AE): perfect. they asked specifically about response differences: they rely on Goliath's "stop" behaviour and deterministic sampling.
Mike (Eng): two notes: 1) temperature semantics match but seed/control is different; for deterministic output suggest pinning model + set temperature=0 and use Redwood's rollout pin to a specific model build. 2) stopping tokens: we support the stop array but tokenization differences can cause off-by-one. Add a post-filter on your shim to trim trailing tokens if strict parity required.
Tyler (SE): For streams, we can provide a tiny client lib (JS ~60 lines) that translates events. We usually include that in POC repo.
Sara (Security): From security/enterprise side, BlueHarbor filed an RFP asking for: SOC2 attestation, data residency, KMS integration, and whether inference logs are retained. Short answers: SOC2 yes (we can provide report), data residency: yes in regions, KMS: yes for Private, logs: defaults to 7d for hosted but configurable for Dedicated/Private. I'll attach the standard matrix.
Jamie (AE): pricing question: they saw lower per-token cost on Goliath for large-batch embeddings. Can we give a rough delta and recommend Dedicated?
Tyler (SE): Rough guidance: hosted unit price might be slightly higher but overall cost can be lower due to batching + KV caching. For large-batch embedding workloads we recommend Dedicated with sustained commit — gives predictable unit cost and throughput. I'll create two price scenarios: hosted vs dedicated (monthly commit).
Jamie (AE): any enterprise blockers we should flag before the POC kickoff?
Sara (Security): blockers to watch: 1) contract language around data residency & processor/subprocessor list, 2) encryption at rest for model caches (we can support HSM in Private), 3) security questionnaire items about incident response times — we have 24/7 SLA options but need to confirm level in SOW.
Mike (Eng): also watch prompt templating: some customers embed vendor-specific tokens in templates. We can add an automated check in the shim that warns about vendor-only tokens. Saves weird failures.
Jamie (AE): timeline: can we run a 2-week POC? Week 1: shim + sample workload, Week 2: compare outputs and perf. BlueHarbor wants a simple migration guide for their frontend/backend engineers.
Tyler (SE): doable. I'll spin up a repo + sample shim and examples. Tagging @deploy-bot to provision a short-lived Dedicated node pool for perf tests (48h).
deploy-bot: Provision request accepted. Pool: redwood-poc-blueharbor-48h created in us-west-2. Credentials posted to secure vault.
Sara (Security): I'll start the questionnaire draft. Need a point of contact at BlueHarbor for encryption/KMS decisions.
Jamie (AE): POC kickoff scheduled Mon 10am PT. I'll send invites and include a link to the repo when Tyler posts it. Thanks :thumbsup:
Tyler (SE): I'll aim to have the initial shim and README by EOD today.
Jamie (AE): Awesome. Action items: Tyler (repo + shim), Sara (questionnaire draft + matrix), Mike (edge cases: tokenization + stop handling), Jamie (customer coordination + calendar).
Jamie (AE): cc'ing BlueHarbor contact in the next message.
